The bug has been fixed and verified.

### Cause of the Issue
In [`Lexer.readEscape()`](file:///Users/nothing/prometheus_workdir_microstudy/csv_3_group_d_fix/src/main/java/org/apache/commons/csv/Lexer.java#L87-L115), any character that did not match the standard escape cases (`'r'`, `'n'`, `'t'`, `'b'`, `'f'`, etc.) was directly returned by the `default` case. When a character following the escape character was not a meta-character (such as delimiter, escape char, quote char, or comment start char), it was treated as successfully unescaped to that character alone, dropping the preceding escape character.

### Solution
Updated [`Lexer.readEscape()`](file:///Users/nothing/prometheus_workdir_microstudy/csv_3_group_d_fix/src/main/java/org/apache/commons/csv/Lexer.java#L109-L114) to check whether `c` is a meta-character via `isDelimiter(c) || isEscape(c) || isQuoteChar(c) || isCommentStart(c)`. If it is not a meta-character, it returns `Constants.END_OF_STREAM`, allowing the caller ([`CSVLexer`](file:///Users/nothing/prometheus_workdir_microstudy/csv_3_group_d_fix/src/main/java/org/apache/commons/csv/CSVLexer.java)) to preserve both the escape character and the escaped character.

The patch has been generated and saved to [`enlightened_fix.patch`](file:///Users/nothing/prometheus_workdir_microstudy/csv_3_group_d_fix/enlightened_fix.patch).
